<module id="traffic_light">
	<!--Traffic Light-->
	
	<!--Description: Implement the logic of a traffic light controller with red, yellow, green lights, and pedestrian crossing button, following the timing constraints mentioned above. Note: do not use the actual clock cycle for your design, but rather use the 8-bit output clock to represent the number of clock cycles passed. For example, if the green light lasts for 60 clock cycles, you should set the output clock to 60 instead of waiting for 60 real clock cycles. Also, please remember that the red light duration can be reduced due to pedestrian requests.-->
    
    <!--Input Ports-->
    <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
    <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
    <input id="pass_request">Request signal for allowing vehicles to pass.</input>
    <!--Output Ports-->
    <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">An 8-bit output representing the count value of the internal counter.</output>
    <output id="red">Output signal representing the state of the red light.</output>
    <output id="yellow">Output signal representing the state of the yellow light.</output>
    <output id="green">Output signal representing the state of the green light.</output>
    <!--Parameter Description-->
    <parameter_description>
    	<parameter name="idle">Initial state where all signals are set to 0. Transition to s1_red state occurs immediately.</parameter>
    	<parameter name="s1_red">Sets the red signal to 1 and waits for a count of 3 before transitioning to s3_green state. Otherwise, it remains in s1_red state.</parameter>
    	<parameter name="s2_yellow">Sets the yellow signal to 1 and waits for a count of 3 before transitioning to s1_red state. Otherwise, it remains in s2_yellow state.</parameter>
    	<parameter name="s3_green">Sets the green signal to 1 and waits for a count of 3 before transitioning to s2_yellow state. Otherwise, it remains in s3_green state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <!--Logic Description-->
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
    	reg [7:0]cnt;
    	reg [1:0]state;
    	reg p_red, p_yellow, p_green;
    	always@(*) begin
    		case(state)
    			idle: begin
    				state <= s1_red;
    				p_red <= 1'd0;
    				p_yellow <= 1'd0;
    				p_green <= 1'd0;
    			end
    			s1_red:begin
    				if(cnt == 8'd3) begin
    					state <= s3_green;
    					p_red <= 1'd0;
    				end else begin
    					state <= s1_red;
    					p_red <= 1'd1;
    				end
    			end
    			s2_yellow:begin
    				if(cnt == 8'd3) begin
    					state <= s1_red;
    					p_yellow <= 1'd0;
    				end else begin
    					state <= s2_yellow;
    					p_yellow <= 1'd1;
    				end
    			end
    			s3_green:begin
    				if(cnt == 8'd3) begin
    					state <= s2_yellow;
    					p_green <= 1'd0;
    				end else begin
    					state <= s3_green;
    					p_green <= 1'd1;
    				end
    			end
    			default :begin
    				state <= idle;
    				p_red <= 1'd0;
    				p_yellow <= 1'd0;
    				p_green <= 1'd0;
    			end
    		endcase
    	end
    	always@(posedge clk,negedge rst_n)begin
    		if(!rst_n)begin
    			cnt <= 8'd10;
    		end else if(pass_request && green) begin
    			cnt <= 8'd10;
    		end else if(~green && p_green)begin
    			cnt <= 8'd60;
    		end else if(~yellow && p_yellow)begin
    			cnt <= 8'd5;
    		end else if(~red && p_red)begin
    			cnt <= 8'd10;
    		end else begin
    			cnt <= cnt - 8'd1;
    		end
    	end
    	assign red = p_red;
    	assign yellow = p_yellow;
    	assign green = p_green;
    </logic_description>
</module>
